The brief

Portfolio for Mara Lindqvist, a documentary wedding photographer in Gothenburg. Quiet and editorial. The six grid tiles are recent weddings; show the couple's names and the venue when you hover a tile. The hero photo is the most recent wedding.

How the model read the sketch

The sketch is a one-page photographer portfolio: a top bar with a round logo and three nav links, a hero with a large photo on the left and a two-line headline, short paragraph and 'hire me' button on the right, a 'selected work' label over a 3×2 grid of image tiles, and a thin footer bar. Built as a dark, editorial page for Mara Lindqvist with serif headlines and wedding titles that appear when a tile is hovered or focused.

circle + 'logo', then 'work about contact' at righttop full-width barHeader with a round 'M' monogram, the name 'Mara Lindqvist', and a three-link navLinks go to #work, #about, #contact — all present. The name text hides below 420px so the bar fits at 360px.
'big photo' box with an Xhero, left ~60%Hero figure (tinted placeholder, 5:3) for the most recent wedding — Elin & Jonas at Gunnebo Slott, September 2026Caption line names the intended image; swap for the real frame.
two thick lines, three thin lines, 'hire me' buttonhero, right columnTwo-line serif headline, one short paragraph, 'Hire me' button linking to #contactThis column carries id='about' so the About nav link lands on the bio.
'selected work' + 3×2 grid of X boxesbelow hero, full widthSection #work with a 3-column grid of six wedding tiles (2 columns under 880px, 1 under 540px)Each tile holds the couple's names (serif) and venue (small sans) in a figcaption revealed on hover/focus; always visible on touch devices.
thin full-width barbottomSingle-row footer with id='contact': email, phone, Instagram, locationKept as thin as drawn; the contact details live here rather than in a separate section.

Gaps it filled

  • Red margin note 'dark + moody, serif headlines, titles appear on hover' treated as instructions, not page content.
  • Palette: warm near-black ground, parchment text, and a single fog-blue accent (Gothenburg west-coast weather) used only for hover titles and focus rings.
  • Type: Cormorant Garamond for headlines and couple names, Instrument Sans for everything else.
  • Six fictional recent weddings at real Gothenburg-area venues (Marstrand, Trädgårdsföreningen, Nääs, Styrsö, Tjolöholm, Slottsskogen) dated May–August 2026; hero is September 2026.
  • Tiles are focusable figures so keyboard users can reveal the title; in the real site each would link to the wedding's gallery.
  • No About or Contact sections drawn, so #about targets the hero bio column and #contact targets the footer, keeping the sketch's structure intact.
  • No JavaScript needed: hover/focus reveal and responsive behaviour are pure CSS.

The brief

Operations dashboard for Pedalhub, a bike-share operator in Lyon. Used on big screens in the depot during the day. The chart is rides per hour for today; the table is the last few rides with station, duration, and fare. Use believable numbers for a city of 500 bikes.

How the model read the sketch

The sketch is a classic admin dashboard: dark-free sidebar nav on the left, a top bar with search, a date control and a round control, four KPI tiles, a wide rides-per-hour line chart beside a top-stations list, and a recent-rides table across the bottom. I built it as a single-page Pedalhub operations screen tuned for a wall display: oversized KPI figures, large table type, high-contrast light surface on a dark sidebar.

Numbers: 1,431 rides so far, 463/500 bikes in service, €2,718 revenue, 14 min 20 s average trip.
rides per hour (wide box with curve)middle row, left ~3/4inline-SVG line chart 06:00–22:00, solid line + area for actual hours up to now, dashed line for the typical-weekday remainder, 'now' marker at 16:00Shape mirrors the sketch: morning peak (214 at 08:00), midday dip, higher evening peak (232 at 18:00). Each point carries a <title> for hover/focus and a visually hidden data table backs the SVG.

red note: 'big numbers, readable from across the room'margin, outside frameinstruction, not renderedDrove the type scale: KPI figures 72–128px, table and list body 20–24px on large screens, strong contrast.

Marks it wasn't sure about

MarkWent withCould also be

fourth table column (sketch only labels the table 'recent rides')ride end time as the first columnbike ID

Gaps it filled

  • Fleet of 500 bikes at roughly 3 rides per bike per day: ~1,430 rides by 16:40, ~2,000 expected by close.
  • Fares follow a Lyon-style scheme: €1.80 for a casual ride up to 30 min, €3.60 beyond, annual pass rides shown as 'Pass'.
  • Station names are real Lyon/Villeurbanne locations (Part-Dieu Villette, Bellecour, Hôtel de Ville, Perrache, Charpennes, etc.).
  • Current time fixed at 16:40 for the static data; a small script updates the clock and date in the top bar but all figures are static HTML.
  • Chart shows actual rides through 16:00 and a dashed typical-weekday line for the rest of the day so the evening peak is anticipated by the depot.
  • Light main surface with a dark sidebar chosen because the screen is used in daylight; no ambient animation added because none was drawn.

The brief

Home screen of Simmer, a weeknight recipe app. Render it as a single phone-width screen centred on the page, not a desktop website. Tonight's pick is a 25-minute miso salmon. The chips filter by time and diet.

How the model read the sketch

The sketch is a single phone screen: greeting header with avatar, a search field, a scrolling chip row, a large 'tonight's pick' image card, a '30 min or less' list of two thumbnail rows, and a four-icon tab bar. I built it as one centred 390px phone screen for Simmer, with working time/diet filter chips and a tap-to-open bottom sheet for the miso salmon pick.

Gaps it filled

  • Screen is 390×844 inside a dark bezel on larger viewports; under 430px wide the screen fills the viewport with no bezel.
  • User name 'Maya' and initials invented for the greeting; weekday is computed from the device clock with 'Tonight' as fallback.
  • Tonight's pick is fixed to the miso salmon regardless of chip state; chips filter only the '30 min or less' list.
  • The two list recipes are a 20-minute chickpea & spinach curry (veggie, vegan) and a 28-minute lemon-garlic chicken orzo so each chip visibly changes the list.
  • Tab bar buttons other than Home are inert in this prototype; no links to screens that were not built.
  • Images are inline SVG illustrations rather than photos.

The brief

Move the three plan cards directly under the nav so pricing is the first thing people see, with the hero below them. Add a short reviews strip with three customer quotes between the hero and the footer. Remove the 'How it works' section. Keep the nav, the plan cards themselves, the palette, and the footer exactly as they are.

How the model read the sketch

The sketch reorders the Fernway landing page: nav, then the three plan cards, then the hero (text left, image right), then a new three-column reviews strip with round avatars, then the footer. I moved the plans section above the hero, removed 'How it works' and its styles, added a reviews strip built from the site's existing tokens, and left the nav, plan cards, palette and footer untouched apart from retargeting two links that pointed at the removed section.

What it changed

  • Moved the complete #plans section above the .hero section; increased .plans top padding from 1rem to 3rem.
  • Removed the #how section, its CSS (.how, .how-grid, .step, .step-icon) and its responsive rule.

Gaps it filled

  • Reviews use three short, specific quotes from fictional customers with name, plan and city; avatars are initials in green-tint circles rather than photos.
  • Reviews section is headed 'What members say' with no separate intro paragraph, keeping the strip short as the brief requests.

The brief

Keep the layout. Switch to a dark theme suited to a depot wall screen, add a date range control to the top bar in place of 'today', make the table columns sortable by clicking the header, and highlight any ride longer than 45 minutes.

How the model read the sketch

Follow-up round on the Pedalhub operations dashboard: same sidebar + topbar + KPI row + chart/stations row + recent-rides table, now in a dark palette tuned for a depot wall screen, with a from–to date range control in the top bar, click-to-sort table headers, and amber highlighting on rides over 45 minutes.

What it changed

  • Switched the palette to a dark theme: deep green-grey background, dark surfaces, light text, brighter green and amber accents; chart, bars, badges, inputs and hover states recoloured to match (color-scheme: dark for native controls).
  • Replaced the 'Today · Sun 11 Oct' select in the top bar with a from → to date range control (two date inputs in one pill, calendar icon, 'to' input min-bound to 'from').
  • Made the four table headers sortable buttons with aria-sort and visible sort arrows; added vanilla JS sorting on data-sort values (time, route text, minutes, fare) and a live region announcing the sort.
  • Added a highlight rule for rides over 45 minutes (amber left rule, tinted row, bold amber duration with a '45+' badge) driven by a data-long attribute; updated two sample rows to exceed 45 minutes and added a footnote explaining the highlight.
  • Bumped the large-screen type scale slightly for wall-screen legibility; everything else (layout, ids, copy, KPIs, chart data, stations, nav) left as it was.

Gaps it filled

  • A wall screen is viewed from a distance, so the base font scales up further on very wide screens (21px at 1900px, 23px at 2500px) and contrast is kept high: light text on deep green-grey rather than pure black.
  • To make the highlight visible, the sample data now contains two rides over 45 minutes: Perrache → Jean Macé at 52 min (€3.70 under the stated tariff) and Guillotière → Confluence at 47 min on a pass.
  • Sorting: first click sorts ascending, second click flips to descending; 'Ended' starts descending (newest first) as in the previous result. Pass rides sort as €0.00 in the Fare column.
  • Changing the date range does not refetch data in a static prototype; the control updates the chart subtitle and the table footnote so the chosen range is visible.
